story_type: car carrier on fire far offshore, crew abandons ship in a lifeboat, picked up by a passing ship
hook: On fire 300 miles out, with 3,048 cars inside.
narration: This ship caught fire with three thousand forty eight vehicles inside, about three hundred miles south of Adak, Alaska.
Seventy of the vehicles on the six hundred foot Morning Midas were fully electric.
A car carrier is a floating parking garage, deck after open deck, so a fire on board has room to spread.
All twenty two crew members left the burning ship in a lifeboat.
The next day, a Coast Guard C-130J crew flew over. Smoke was still pouring out of the ship.
outcome: All twenty two crew members were rescued by the motor vessel Cosco Hellas, with no reported injuries.

location_card.place: North Pacific, south of Adak, Alaska

title: Car carrier on fire 300 miles out
description:
The 600-foot cargo ship Morning Midas caught fire about 300 miles south of Adak, Alaska, in June 2025 with 3,048 vehicles aboard. All 22 crew members evacuated in a lifeboat and were rescued by the motor vessel Cosco Hellas.

Footage: U.S. Coast Guard video, U.S. Coast Guard Arctic District, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/965531/coast-guard-conducts-overflight-vessel-fire-offshore-adak-alaska
